A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRAP² research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated results.

before.justification: v1 reports original standalone and merging experiments on eight vision benchmarks, together with scaling, interpolation, and correlation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds mathematical-reasoning evaluations, LoRA-variant experiments, recovery attacks, and training-cost measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the generic TRAP² objective remain unchanged. The new LLM instantiation uses off-nominal loss weighting w(s) = 1/sqrt(s) instead of the default 1/s (Appendix D.3), a limited adaptation of the training loss.

E1.justification: v2 extends the original eight vision benchmarks to GSM8K and ASDiv mathematical word problems using Llama-3.1-8B. This adds language generation and mathematical reasoning to the previously visual task coverage; all original datasets remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds element-wise ProDistill and post-merge supervised fine-tuning as evaluated recovery methods (Tables 5 and 14), substantially extending the adversarial comparison beyond merging operators. Existing protection baselines and merging methods remain; class-stratified RegMean/CoM comparisons omitted from the revised main table are retained in Table 13.

E3.justification: New protocols include numeric-answer exact-match evaluation and dataset splits for mathematical reasoning, rank-32 Llama adapters, QLoRA/DoRA configurations, and recovery using 64 held-out examples per dataset. Appendix C.4 also introduces shared-target and matched-wall-clock training-cost comparisons. These additions do not establish changes to the retained vision experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds recovery stress tests, checks protection under QLoRA and DoRA, and analyzes training overhead and dataset-dependent convergence. Appendix C.2 adds two qualitative LLM examples showing degenerate merged outputs. The original scaling, pairwise interpolation, and correlation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 newly states that the ASDiv split uses a fixed random seed, without specifying its value. No additional repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported; the existing eight target-task trials and correlation reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds LLM and LoRA-variant curves, qualitative outputs, recovery scores, and timing/memory results. New recovery comparisons report protected versus unprotected accuracy of 49.153% versus 73.823% for ProDistill and 45.496% versus 56.859% for SFT. Table 1 corrects the ViT-B/32 fine-tuned average from 87.994% to 88.119%, with constituent scores unchanged. Other retained benchmark tables preserve their results.

T1.justification: The formal TRAP² objective, assumptions, Theorems A.1/A.2/A.4, Corollary A.3, and their proofs are unchanged apart from numbering and references. The added ProDistill formula documents the comparator without extending the theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contributions retain the same training-time unmergeability claim. The concluding limitations now explicitly qualify architecture-agnosticity as a property of the objective and formulation, rather than coverage of every architecture or deployment setting.

C2.justification: v1 leaves data-driven recovery to future work; v2 interprets new tests as evidence of resistance to recovery. It adds explanations of training-cost variability, including the Cars slowdown, and limitations concerning tuning, architectural validation, base-model drift, and permission-aware composition. The averaging proxy is clarified. However, the new interpretation that mathematical-reasoning standalone utility is preserved conflicts with the GSM8K endpoints in Figure 9.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds mathematical prompts, answer extraction and splits, the Llama checkpoint and training settings, QLoRA quantization settings, DoRA configuration, and recovery sample counts. Appendix C.4 identifies the RTX A6000 hardware and documents timing and memory measurements. These substantially expand reproducibility information while retaining the original vision details.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations supporting ProDistill, GSM8K/ASDiv, Llama, QLoRA/DoRA, zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting, and the Datasets library. The main related-work discussion and positioning against PaRaMS and Merge-Lock remain largely unchanged. Publication and bibliographic updates do not introduce different prior works.

P1.justification: The established narrative is retained, with localized wording corrections and restructuring of Section 6 into generalization, data-aware robustness, and additional analysis. Appendices C and D gain corresponding subsections; affiliations, publication text, and acknowledgements also change. Most existing prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 9–10 and Tables 6, 8, and 14, substantially expanding the experimental displays. Table 5 is reorganized into merging and recovery groups. Existing Figures 5–6 exchange numbers and positions; the averaging-proxy caption is clarified, and Figure 8's interpolation-direction formula is corrected without changing its plotted results.

improvement.justification: The recovery tests address a question v1 explicitly left open, while the cost measurements and clearer applicability limits improve practical assessment. However, v2 claims comparable standalone mathematical-reasoning utility even though Figure 9 shows roughly 20% protected GSM8K accuracy versus 60% unprotected at the respective standalone endpoints. This unresolved discrepancy weakens the new generalization evidence and limits the overall quality gain.
